text:
rana: Short sync — proposing 'stitch-update' as the private distro upgrade flow for VPC/on-prem customers. Main goals: predictable upgrades for field, clear ownership for peering/IPs, and an offline-friendly path.

julio: Love the name. Quick Q: do we require customer to opt into "net-claim" metadata before upgrade? Some customers want us to auto-detect.

anya: For airgapped sites we must support: (a) offline delta bundles, (b) deterministic preflight, (c) compact rollback snapshot. Customers asked for a dry-run that simulates route changes without touching BGP/peers.

sam: Concrete ask from field: preserve static peering IPs and any nodePort mappings during upgrade. Also a single command dry-run and an explainable conflict report.

rana: Draft GA acceptance (lean):
- offline delta bundles with signed manifest + size/sha checks
- redwoodctl plan-upgrade --bundle <file> --dry-run -> prints plan + conflicts
- net-claim metadata (optional) but preflight must surface missing claims and recommended resolution
- IP-preserve mode: `--maintain-ip-mapping` (best-effort, documented failure modes)
- phased rollout knob: --canary-percent + automatic health gating
- explicit rollback: `redwoodctl rollback --to snapshot:<id>`
- ops runbook + customer checklist + 2hr SLA for field support response

julio: On net-claim, suggest this annotation shape: `net_claims=[{"subnet":"10.0.3.0/24","owner":"netops@cust.co","preserve_ips":true}]` — keep it JSON-ish but stored as a string in the agent manifest so older agents ignore unknown keys.

anya: Prototype manifest suggestion (single-line string in bundle index, keep tiny):
```json
{"stitch_version":"1","components":["agent","runtime"],"deltas":[{"path":"delta-2026-03.bin","sha256":"..."}],"net_claims":[]}
```
Keep manifest parsing minimal (no recursive schemas).

sam: UX notes: field wants a machine-parsable output when dry-run succeeds/fails, plus a human summary. Example: `redwoodctl plan-upgrade --bundle stitch.tar.gz --dry-run --out ./plan.json`

rana: Edge rules for multiple owners: use most-specific prefix match (subnet-level overrides VPC-level). If overlap/conflict detected, preflight must return a conflict_id and a suggested resolution snippet. Example resolution snippet: `redwoodctl set-net-claim --subnet 10.0.3.0/24 --owner netops@cust.co`

julio: Security: signed manifests only, agent will verify cert chain. For offline verification we must ship root cert with the bundle or provide offline CA fingerprint.

anya: Testing requirements: add a peering-preserve test to the nightly QA matrix that runs upgrade on a 3-node cluster with a simulated external peer (validate IPs and port mappings). We should also include a synthetic traffic ramp to ensure health gating works.

sam: Field ops checklist (short):
- confirm net-claim for all subnets
- run dry-run and inspect `conflicts` section
- schedule canary window and monitor metric X (peer-error-rate)
- if conflicts, apply suggested resolution or abort
- if upgrade fails, run `redwoodctl rollback --to snapshot:<id>` and open ticket with attachment of `plan.json`

rana: Responsibility split: @julio -> spec net-claim shape + crypto verification (EOD Fri); @anya -> manifest/agent minimal parsing + QA test harness (next week); @sam -> field checklist + sample commands + customer-facing wording (tomorrow). I'll compile a one-pager and set up a 30m review with two customers Wed.

upgrade-bot: Created draft doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/stitch-upgrade (shared: product, field)

anya: One more thought: include a `--simulate-peer-loss` flag in dry-run to surface risk of BGP flaps. Field wants this for fragile peering configs.

julio: ok to include but make it opt-in and default off. Also add a TTL for claimed routes so claims don't persist forever if customer forgets to clear them.

sam: Can we add a tiny example in docs for preserving nodePort mappings? i.e., mapping table before/after so netops can verify.

rana: Yes. I'll add mapping example + minimal troubleshooting notes. Final: will post agenda and capture AIs. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
